done_when: Close starts the review at the same time as its tests, so a round takes about as long as the slower of the two; a red test or a P0/P1 finding still stops the round, and both results are reported together. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Functional. The new local-test guard at this line runs only after the new release is on the default branch. During `forge upgrade`, the new release runs `close` on an upgrade pull request, but the pull request workflow checks out the base branch and installs its older Forge version (`src/forge/prcheck.py:100–121`). The v1.2.2 checker (`tests/fixtures/forge-v1.2.2/src/forge/prcheck.py:169–180`) ignores saved test failures. In a supported repo without a required `tests` check where draft pull requests are unavailable, a clean review and red local test therefore leave the upgrade PR mergeable. The new earlier-adoption test merges the synced release into `main` before invoking this check, so it does not cover the upgrade PR.
findings.title: Upgrade PRs with red local tests can pass the previous release's check
